paper.title: No Internal Regret via Neighborhood Watch

settings.name_in_paper: Finite partial-monitoring game under the local observability condition (non-stochastic opponent)
unmapped: learner knows the loss matrix L and signal matrix H
regret measured against departure functions (internal / local internal regret)
no action is completely dominated and the best-response cells form a non-degenerate partition
settings.definition_quote: Imagine playing a repeated zero-sum game against an opponent (column player) where the loss is defined by a given matrix $L\in \reals^{N\times M}$. ... we (the row player) do not observe the moves of the opponent and instead receive some signal given by the known matrix $H\in \Sigma^{N\times M}$ ... The game is called locally observable if $\ell_i-\ell_j \in \text{Im}~S^\tr_{(i,j)}$ for all neighboring actions $i,j$.

symbols.v_bar: max over neighboring pairs (i,j) of ||v_(i,j)||_inf, where l_j - l_i = S_(i,j)^T v_(i,j)

conditions: no action is completely dominated; best-response cells form a non-degenerate partition
tuning: gamma = 0 (proof yields extra term T N gamma lbar)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Local internal regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg} is bounded as \sup_{\phi}\E \left\{ \sum_{t=1}^T (e_{I_t}-e_{\phi(I_t)})^\tr L e_{j_t} \right\} \leq 4N\bar{v}\sqrt{6 (\log N) T} where $\bar{v} = \max_{(i,j)} \|v_{(i,j)}\|_\infty$ and supremum is taken over all local departure functions.

results.notes: Local internal regret (sup over local departure functions). Paper's N = number of player actions (K). The proof actually gives 4N vbar sqrt(6 log N T) + T N gamma lbar; theorem statement corresponds to gamma = 0. Section 5 states the same O(sqrt T) holds with random signals (informal).

conditions: no action is completely dominated; best-response cells form a non-degenerate partition

source.quote: Internal regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg} is also bounded as in Theorem~\ref{thm:regret}.

results.notes: Global internal regret (departure functions phi_{i->j}), via Lemma 3.1 (local internal regret = internal regret). Paper claims this implies O(sqrt T) external regret too (informally).
